claim_reviews.claim: h(d)=1 rate decreases 42.1% (d < 10^4) -> 25.7% (10^6) -> 16.70% ([10^9,10^10)) -> 15.35% ([10^10,10^11)); asymptotically -> 0 by genus theory + Erdos-Kac; Cohen-Lenstra's 75.446% applies to Prob(h_odd = 1), not Prob(h = 1).
claim_reviews.evidence: The two large-range rates match the committed logs exactly (16.7047%, 15.3530%). The structural argument is correct mathematics: h = 1 forces trivial 2-part, genus theory ties the 2-rank to the number of prime factors of the discriminant, and omega(d) ~ log log d makes such discriminants density-zero — so Pr(h=1) -> 0 while C-L governs the odd part. The 2026-04-01 correction note (retracting the original 'non-monotone convergence to 75%') is a documented, transparent fix of a real conceptual error. The small-range values (42.1%, 25.7%) are spot-check claims without committed logs.
claim_reviews.concerns: Residual title/body artifact: the H1 heading still says 'Convergence Is Non-Monotone' while the corrected content says monotone decrease — an editing leftover from the correction.

claim_reviews.claim: Class-number distribution tables (h = 1..16 shares at both ranges; 3|h, 5|h, 7|h vs C-L predictions; power-of-2 share 74.1% -> 73.4%).
claim_reviews.evidence: Every tabulated percentage matches the committed logs to the printed precision, in both ranges; the genus-theory shift deltas (h=8: +0.77 pp, h=16: +0.63 pp) recompute exactly. This is one of the cleanest artifact-to-page correspondences in the project.

sources.reference: Both range logs, histogram blocks (20 lines each, all checked)

claim_reviews.claim: Computational details for the 27B block: ~4.5 hours on 8x B200 at ~82% utilization, ~1.7M disc/sec; random 0.01% PARI/GP subsample with exact agreement.
claim_reviews.evidence: Neither committed log for the [10^10, 10^11) range matches this: run_1e10_1e11.log records 59,527 s (16.5 h) at 459,568 disc/s and v2 records 90,666 s (25.2 h) at 301,731 disc/s. No log matching 4.5 h / 1.7M disc/s exists in the repository, no utilization telemetry is committed, and no PARI/GP subsample validation artifact exists. The scientific results are unaffected (the histograms come from the committed logs), but this performance-and-validation paragraph is unsupported by, and in tension with, the repository record.

sources.reference: run_1e10_1e11.log (59,527 s), run_1e10_1e11_v2.log (90,666 s); no matching 16,200 s log; no PARI validation artifact

claim_reviews.concerns: Either a faster cluster run existed and its log was never committed (violating the preservation rule) or the paragraph is inaccurate.

claim_reviews.evidence: run_1e9_1e10.log: 1,791.2 s = 29.9 min at 1,527,243 disc/s. Matches.

overall_assessment: Scientifically this is among the project's best pages: a real conceptual error was caught, corrected, and documented; the corrected mathematics (genus theory forcing Pr(h=1) -> 0, C-L applying to the odd part) is right; and all forty-plus statistical values I checked match the committed logs exactly across 30 billion discriminants. Two blemishes: the 27B block's performance-and-validation paragraph (4.5 h / 1.7M per sec / PARI subsample) is contradicted by both committed logs and backed by no artifact, and the H1 heading still carries the pre-correction 'Non-Monotone' title.
recommendations: Fix or evidence the 27B performance paragraph (commit the cluster log if one exists; otherwise report the committed 25.2 h run)
Run and commit the promised PARI/GP subsample validation
Update the H1 heading to match the corrected claim
Commit spot-check logs for the small-range (10^4, 10^6) values
certification_justification: The mathematical content and all distribution statistics are fully log-verified at 30-billion scale with an exemplary correction trail; the disputed items concern performance narrative, not results. Silver, with the performance paragraph flagged for repair.
